true_pathology_labels_found.name: grade_label / grade (GlaS)
true_pathology_labels_found.source: data/glas/Warwick_QU_Dataset/Grade.csv, column ' grade (GlaS)' (also already carried into data_manifests/glas_manifest_stage3_finalized.csv as 'grade_label', 0=benign/1=malignant)
true_pathology_labels_found.independent_of_model_prediction: YES for the orientation/order representation (S_DL, phi_DL) -- this label is what the CLASSIFICATION HEAD was trained on, so it is NOT independent of logits/accuracy (already reported in Stage 9/11/14), but the Q-head's (S_DL, phi_DL) output has no direct supervision from this label (Model 3's loss has no term connecting q_head to grade_label) -- association between (S_DL, phi_DL) and grade_label is therefore a non-circular question

true_pathology_labels_found.name: ordinal_grade / grade (Sirinukunwattana et al. 2015)
true_pathology_labels_found.source: data/glas/Warwick_QU_Dataset/Grade.csv, column ' grade (Sirinukunwattana et al. 2015)' -- NOT previously loaded or used anywhere in code/ or code_v2/ (verified by grep)
true_pathology_labels_found.type: 5-level ordinal categorical: healthy < adenomatous < moderately differentiated < moderately-to-poorly differentiated < poorly differentiated (standard disease-severity ordering per the original GlaS grading scheme; verified consistent with grade_label: crosstab shows healthy+adenomatous are 100% benign, the other 3 levels are 100% malignant)
true_pathology_labels_found.independent_of_model_prediction: YES, same reasoning as grade_label -- never used in any loss term

morphology_surrogates_found.name: gland n_pixels (area)
morphology_surrogates_found.independent_of_Q_target: YES -- area is not part of the S_cov/phi_cov eigenvalue-ratio formula that defines the anatomical Q target; a genuinely separate morphology quantity

morphology_surrogates_found.name: n_gland_instances per image
morphology_surrogates_found.independent_of_Q_target: YES -- a count, not an orientation/anisotropy quantity

morphology_surrogates_found.name: n_connected_components / fragmented flag per gland, aggregated to image (fragmented-gland count)
morphology_surrogates_found.independent_of_Q_target: YES -- a topological/segmentation-quality property, not an orientation quantity

morphology_surrogates_found.name: S_cov / phi_cov per gland (and S_contour / phi_contour)
morphology_surrogates_found.independent_of_Q_target: NO -- this IS the literal source of the anatomical Q target used throughout Stages 4/9/11. Any S_DL-vs-S_cov analysis would simply re-run Stage 11's Criterion B under a new label. NOT USED as a confound or endpoint in this stage's primary/morphology analyses -- explicitly excluded per instruction section 9/18.

acquisition_variables_found.name: patient ID
acquisition_variables_found.source: data/glas/Warwick_QU_Dataset/Grade.csv, column 'patient ID' -- NOT previously used anywhere in this project
acquisition_variables_found.level: patient (16 total across all 165 images; 12 distinct patients within the 80 testA+testB images)
acquisition_variables_found.note: CRITICAL CLUSTERING FINDING: 11 of 16 patients contribute images to more than one canonical split (including 2 patients -- IDs 3 and 7 -- who contribute images to BOTH testA and testB). Images are therefore NOT independent observations at the patient level. This is reported and addressed via a pre-specified patient-level robustness check (R1), not ignored.

acquisition_variables_found.name: canonical_split, image_id, image dimensions
acquisition_variables_found.category: C_acquisition_variable, used for stratification/provenance only, not as an endpoint

dataset_capability_audit_summary.explicitly_not_available: No clinically-annotated variables beyond the two grade columns above exist anywhere in the GlaS distribution used by this project (verified by full-column inspection of Grade.csv, the only label source ever used by code/data_prep.py::find_label_csv). No lumen-specific measurements, no scanner metadata, no additional clinical covariates (age, sex, treatment, outcome) exist in this dataset.

representation_variables.source: Frozen Stage 10 Model 3 checkpoint (results_v2/model3/checkpoints/checkpoint_final.pt), inference only, via the EXACT existing pipeline (code_v2/stage9_train_baselines.py::to_tensors/per_patch_scalar_qs, code_v2/stage11_geometric_validation.py::get_predictions) -- no retraining, no architecture change, no new representation invented.

quantities_used.name: S_DL
quantities_used.definition: per-patch predicted order magnitude sqrt(q1_pred^2+q2_pred^2), masked-mean-reduced per patch exactly as in Stage 9/11, then averaged again across all patches within an image (unweighted mean over that image's valid patches) to form ONE value per image -- the natural unit for association with an image-level pathology/morphology variable

quantities_used.name: phi_DL circular dispersion
quantities_used.definition: 1 - |mean_over_patches(exp(i*2*phi_DL))| (circular variance of the mod-pi orientation angle across an image's valid patches, using the same doubled-angle head-tail-symmetric convention as nematic_math.py throughout this project). A derived STATISTIC of the existing phi_DL representation, not a new model output. High value = orientation varies a lot across the image's patches (low consistency); low value = patches agree on orientation.

quantities_deliberately_excluded_as_prim.name: mean phi_DL itself (not dispersion)
quantities_deliberately_excluded_as_prim.reason: phi has no canonical zero reference that is meaningful to compare in aggregate ACROSS different images/glands (only relative/dispersion statistics are frame-independent) -- a population mean of an arbitrary-reference angle is not a scientifically meaningful quantity, so it is not tested at all (neither primary nor exploratory), rather than silently included and misinterpreted.

quantities_deliberately_excluded_as_prim.name: S_anat / phi_anat (the anatomical target itself)
quantities_deliberately_excluded_as_prim.reason: using this as either the representation variable or a confound would either duplicate Stage 11's Criterion B under a new label, or adjust for the very quantity the model is meant to predict -- excluded per instruction section 9/18.

population_and_unit_of_analysis.primary_population: testA + testB pooled, 80 canonical held-out images (1470+613=2083 patches, exactly Stage 11's population, no exclusions -- fragmented testB images retained)
population_and_unit_of_analysis.unit_of_analysis_primary: IMAGE (n=80) -- pathology/morphology labels are recorded at image level; patch-level pseudoreplication is explicitly avoided by aggregating S_DL and phi_DL-dispersion to one value per image before any statistical test
population_and_unit_of_analysis.unit_of_analysis_robustness: PATIENT (n=12 distinct patients within the 80 held-out images) -- reported as a pre-specified sensitivity check given the clustering finding above
population_and_unit_of_analysis.testA_testB_reported_separately: YES, in addition to the pooled analysis, exactly mirroring Stage 11's convention

primary_analyses.hypothesis: Non-directional: does image-level mean S_DL differ between benign and malignant images? No direction (higher-in-malignant or higher-in-benign) is assumed before analysis.
primary_analyses.effect_size: Cohen's d (and Glass's Delta using benign as reference group, for consistency with this project's established effect-size convention)
primary_analyses.ci: bootstrap 95% CI on the difference of group means, resampled at the IMAGE level, n_boot=2000, seed=42
primary_analyses.unit_of_analysis: image (n=80, pooled; also testA n=60 and testB n=20 separately)

primary_analyses.hypothesis: Non-directional: is image-level mean S_DL associated (monotonically) with ordinal histological grade?
primary_analyses.ci: bootstrap 95% CI, image-level resampling, n_boot=2000, seed=42

primary_analyses.hypothesis: Non-directional: does within-image orientation consistency differ between benign and malignant images?
primary_analyses.ci: bootstrap 95% CI, image-level resampling, n_boot=2000, seed=42

primary_analyses.hypothesis: Non-directional: is within-image orientation consistency associated with ordinal grade?
primary_analyses.ci: bootstrap 95% CI, image-level resampling, n_boot=2000, seed=42

confounding_analysis.description: OLS regression of image-level mean S_DL on grade_label (0/1) + mean gland area (covariate), examining whether grade_label's coefficient/significance changes materially after adjusting for area. Run regardless of P1's outcome (pre-specified unconditionally, not triggered by seeing P1's result).

robustness_analyses.description: Patient-level aggregation sensitivity check: re-aggregate S_DL to one value per PATIENT (mean over that patient's images' image-level S_DL values) within testA+testB (n=12 distinct patients), and re-examine P1's grade_label association at this coarser unit. Reported descriptively (Mann-Whitney U + effect size where n permits), with explicit acknowledgment that n=12 is likely underpowered -- this is a sensitivity/transparency check, not a claim of a definitive patient-level result.

exploratory_analyses_policy: Any analysis not listed above that is run after the primary/morphology/confound/robustness results are seen MUST be labeled EXPLORATORY in every output artifact and MUST NOT be used to justify a primary conclusion.

multiple_testing.correction: Holm-Bonferroni, applied across exactly these 4 pre-specified primary pathology tests (pooled testA+testB results only; testA/testB-separate and morphology/confound/robustness results are reported with raw p-values, explicitly labeled as not part of the corrected family, per instruction section 11's 'small number of explicitly pre-specified hypotheses' allowance).

explicit_prohibitions_restated: No directional hypothesis (e.g. 'malignant -> higher S') is assumed anywhere in this matrix -- all tests are two-sided.
No image, gland, or patch is excluded beyond what Stage 9's original >=10% valid-coverage patch-inclusion rule already applied (frozen, unchanged, applied identically to every prior stage).
No statistical test is chosen after seeing which produces the strongest result -- all tests above are fixed before any S_DL/phi_DL computation in this stage.
S_anat/phi_anat and S_cov/phi_cov are never used as a representation variable, endpoint, or confound in this stage.
